zoe-px: Quick thread: proposing a compact nav IA + deep-link normalization. Goals: make shared links human-friendly, stable across small IA changes, and accessible. Sketch: canonical path segments (`/console/models/:id/deployments`) + server-side canonicalization & Link headers. Questions: how do we handle user-specific sidebar state (collapsed groups) when someone opens a shared link?

matt-eng: My take: keep canonical urls independent of user prefs. If a shared link targets a nested item and the user's sidebar is collapsed, auto-expand that group on load but do NOT change user preference persistently. That prevents share links from mutating personal settings. Also: return `Link: <canonical-url>; rel="canonical"` header for crawlers.

jenny-a11y: Accessibility: when auto-expanding a group for a deep link, announce the change politely (`aria-live="polite"`) and move focus to the H1 only. Do not shove focus into the nav. Ensure skip-to-content is visible on focus. `aria-current="page"` on active leaf element. Also ensure focus order remains logical when groups expand.

sasha-dev: Implementation notes: 1) Server: accept legacy `?tab=` and hashes; respond with 301 -> canonical path for bots and offer a quick client-side redirect for browsers that also records the original incoming URL in analytics. 2) Client: on mount, if we see an incoming alias/legacy query, map to canonical and `history.replaceState` to avoid double entries in back/forward. 3) Keep a small mapping table in the routing layer so left-nav highlight is computed from routePattern -> navKey (not string startsWith).

zoe-px: Copy + social preview: breadcrumbs should be human readable: "Models > ResNet-XL > Deployments". H1s should be friendly like "Model details". For social previews (when someone shares a link in Slack/email), we should provide OG tags with short summary (model name + resource type). That means server-side rendering of OG metadata for canonical paths.

matt-eng: We can server-render minimal OG meta (title, description, image) for key resource paths. Also emit `canonical` Link header and return 301 for legacy query routes when we can. For client redirects use `history.replaceState` so hitting back doesn't bounce to the legacy URL. Record both `incoming_raw_url` and `canonical_url` in telemetry so experiments and attribution preserve context.

jenny-a11y: Minor a11y nits: 1) Ensure crumb separators are visible to sighted users but announced properly to SR users; 2) use `role="navigation"` and `aria-label` for left nav; 3) keyboard users should be able to collapse/expand groups with Enter/Space and see `aria-expanded` update.

sasha-dev: Edgecases: 1) Hash anchors like `/models/12#perf` should be handled client-side (SSR returns canonical path, client scrolls after hydrate). 2) If a share link points to a resource the user lacks permission for, show a clear accessible error and provide a link to request access. 3) For compact share links (short urls), treat them as separate backend mappings and always expand to canonical for OG/meta.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: branch `nav/normalize-ogs` -> staging deploy 2026-05-12T04:00:00Z. CI: lint + a11y smoke tests.

zoe-px: Next steps: I'll update the IA mocks to show auto-expand behavior and provide copy for breadcrumbs + OG templates. Sasha 
did you want a short routing spec I can include?

sasha-dev: Yes please  include the mapping table idea and the replaceState behavior. I'll draft the small server-side redirect table. Will sync in PR. Thanks! :wave:
